newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Gaddafi back in Libya after defiant flight.
newsitem.headline: Gaddafi back in Libya after defiant flight.

text.p: Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi on Saturday returned to Tripoli after a defiant flight to Niger and Nigeria despite the United Nations air embargo over the Lockerbie affair.

The Libyan state-run television monitored in Tunis showed Gaddafi emerging from a Libyan Arab Airlines Boeing at Tripoli airport, back from Niger and Nigeria where he led prayers for the Moslem new year.
Hundreds of followers acclaimed Gaddafi on the tarmac while he raised arms as a sign of victory for his defiant three-day trip.

Gaddafi's trip to West Africa was in apparent defiance of a 1992 United Nations embargo on flights from his state. The ban was imposed for Libya's failure to extradite two agents linked to the bombing of the Pan Am flight over Lockerbie in 1988 and four agents linked to the 1989 bombing of a French airliner.

In Washington, a State Department spokesman said on Thursday the United States was investigating reports the flight embargo had been broken and if it had been, the matter would be pursued in the U.N. Security Council and sanctions committee. A U.S. official said military action was not being considered.
Gaddafi's last trip abroad was by land to Tunisia in October 1996. He violated the ban when a Libyan-registered plane flew him to Cairo and back to attend an Arab summit in June 1996.
